report_name: Ransomware Roundup: Qilin, Gammax, Genesis, and Others Claim Victims

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: A prominent ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group that listed the Belgian logistics firm ADPO on its data leak site as part of a double extortion attack.

threat_actors.name: Gammax
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed an attack on AguAseo, an environmental services company in Panama, using a double extortion model.

threat_actors.name: Genesis
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed responsibility for an attack on Boyum IT Solutions, a Danish software company, using a double extortion model.

threat_actors.name: CMD
threat_actors.description: An emerging hacking group that listed Contact Group, an Australian building services company, on its leak site in a double extortion ransomware attack.

threat_actors.name: Unsafe
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed a breach against Blue Vista Capital Management, a U.S. real estate investment firm, likely involving sensitive financial records.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: As part of the double extortion model, threat actors exfiltrated large amounts of sensitive data by uploading it to attacker-controlled cloud storage services before encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware payloads were deployed across victim networks to encrypt files, as part of the double extortion strategy.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators used the command `vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet` to delete Volume Shadow Copies, preventing easy file recovery from local backups.

malware.name: Qilin Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware used by the Qilin group to encrypt files on the victim's (ADPO) network as part of a double extortion attack.

malware.name: Gammax Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware used by the Gammax group to encrypt files on the victim's (AguAseo) network as part of a double extortion attack.

malware.name: Genesis Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware used by the Genesis group to encrypt files on the victim's (Boyum IT Solutions) network as part of a double extortion attack.

malware.name: CMD Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware used by the CMD group to encrypt files on the victim's (Contact Group) network as part of a double extortion attack.

malware.name: Unsafe Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware used by the Unsafe group to encrypt files on the victim's (Blue Vista Capital Management) network as part of a double extortion attack.

tools.name: rclone
tools.description: Legitimate command-line tool for managing cloud storage, abused by ransomware groups to exfiltrate large volumes of data before encryption.

tools.name: megacmd.exe
tools.description: Legitimate command-line tool for interacting with MEGA cloud storage, abused by ransomware groups to exfiltrate data.

identities.name: ADPO
identities.description: A Belgian logistics and chemical supply chain company targeted by the Qilin ransomware group.

identities.name: AguAseo
identities.description: An environmental services company in Panama targeted by the Gammax ransomware group.

identities.name: Boyum IT Solutions
identities.description: A Danish software company specializing in SAP Business One solutions, targeted by the Genesis ransomware group.

identities.name: Contact Group
identities.description: An Australian building services and electrical contracting company targeted by the 'CMD' ransomware group.

identities.name: Blue Vista Capital Management
identities.description: A U.S.-based real estate investment firm targeted by the 'Unsafe' ransomware group.

indicators.name: Ransomware Exfiltration Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Ransomware Exfiltration Tool Execution
id: 2b1c3d4e-5f6a-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of legitimate cloud sync tools like rclone.exe or megacmd.exe, which are commonly abused by ransomware groups for data exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.breachsense.com/breaches/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.exfiltration
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rclone.exe'
      - '\megacmd.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of legitimate data synchronization tools commonly abused by ransomware actors for data exfiltration prior to encryption.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: f8a1b2c3-d4e5-4f6a-b7c8-d9e0f1a2b3c4
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.breachsense.com/breaches/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the vssadmin.exe utility to delete Volume Shadow Copies, a technique used by ransomware to prevent system recovery.
